tour.name: Chiang Mai Ethical Elephant Sanctuary Private Day: Observe, Feed & Walk with Rescued Elephants
tour.subtitle: A private day with rescued elephants at a responsible sanctuary in the hills north of Chiang Mai, with your own guide and car: watching the herd in a natural setting, preparing their food, walking with them through the forest and learning their stories, with no riding, no bathing shows and no tricks.

highlights: A responsible sanctuary for elephants rescued from logging and tourism
Watching the herd behave naturally in a large valley
Preparing food for the elderly elephants
A walk with the elephants through the forest and along the river
The stories of each elephant from the mahouts and keepers
A Thai lunch at the sanctuary
No riding, no forced bathing and no performances
tour.overview:
Thailand has some 3,800 captive elephants, many of whom once worked in logging until it was banned in 1989, then in tourism, giving rides and performing tricks. Riding and shows harm elephants, which are trained with painful methods and carry loads their spines were not made for. A growing number of sanctuaries now rescue elephants and let them live as naturally as possible, funded by visitors who come to watch, feed and walk with them.

This private day takes you to a responsible sanctuary in the hills north of Chiang Mai, chosen for its welfare standards, with your own guide and car. You watch the elephants graze, dust-bathe and socialise, help prepare food for the older animals, walk with the herd through the forest and along the river, and learn each elephant's story and how you can help protect them.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 8 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Chiang Mai
• Type: private transfer and guide, sanctuary programme
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy to moderate; about 3 km of walking on rural paths

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Mae Taeng valley.
• A rescued elephant herd in a natural environment.
• The sanctuary's food preparation and care.
• Forest and river walks with the elephants.

WHY THIS WORKS
We choose sanctuaries with no riding, no bathing with tourists, small visitor numbers and veterinary care, and travel privately so you set your own pace.

WHO IT SUITS
Animal lovers, families with children and anyone who wants to meet elephants responsibly.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer temples and culture, choose our Doi Suthep and old city tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Visitor numbers are limited and the best sanctuaries book up weeks ahead, especially from November to February. Contact with elephants is decided by the keepers for the animals' wellbeing; it is never guaranteed.

days.name: A day with rescued elephants in the Mae Taeng valley
days.description:
What to expect: a responsible encounter with rescued elephants, with a private guide and car, the sanctuary programme and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel at about 8:00 for the drive north into the Mae Taeng valley, about an hour, past rice fields and forested hills. At the sanctuary, the staff introduce the herd and explain the rules: no riding, no climbing on the elephants, no hugging for selfies, and always following the keepers' lead. You learn how elephants were used in logging and trekking, how the sanctuary rescued its residents – some blind, some with injuries from landmines or years of carrying riders – and how they are cared for.

From a viewing platform and then on foot, you watch the elephants grazing, throwing mud and dust over their backs to protect their skin, playing in the river and interacting with their families. In the food preparation area you help make rice balls with bananas and tamarind for the older elephants who can no longer chew well, and hand out fruit at the feeding platform. After a Thai lunch at the sanctuary, you walk with a small group of elephants and their mahouts through the forest and along the river, at the elephants' pace, watching them forage and bathe on their own terms.

In the afternoon you can visit the sanctuary's other rescued animals, such as dogs and buffaloes, and hear about the conservation work in the region before your driver takes you back to Chiang Mai, arriving at about 16:00.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:00 – Pick-up at your hotel.
09:00 – Arrival at the sanctuary and introduction.
09:30 – Observing the herd.
11:00 – Food preparation and feeding.
12:00 – Lunch.
13:15 – Walk with the elephants.
14:45 – Other rescued animals and conservation talk.
15:00 – Drive back.
16:00 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Contact with elephants depends on each animal's temperament and the keepers' decisions.
• We do not work with places that offer riding, painting or shows.
• Overnight stays at some sanctuaries can be arranged.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, private guide, sanctuary programme, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: donations, drinks, tips.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Can we ride or bathe the elephants?
faq.answer: No. Riding harms elephants, and bathing with tourists stresses them. You observe, feed and walk with them, which is far more rewarding.

faq.question: How do you choose the sanctuary?
faq.answer: We work with sanctuaries that rescue elephants, offer no riding or shows, limit visitor numbers, provide veterinary care and let the animals live in herds.

faq.question: Will we be able to touch the elephants?
faq.answer: Sometimes, at feeding time, when the keepers allow it. Contact is never forced and never guaranteed.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, a Thai lunch at the sanctuary, often vegetarian.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes, it is a wonderful day for children, who learn a lot about animal welfare. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. Viewing platforms are easy to reach, but the walks are on uneven, sometimes muddy paths.

faq.question: How far in advance should we book?
faq.answer: As early as possible: responsible sanctuaries accept few visitors per day and fill up weeks ahead in the high season.

faq.question: What should we bring?
faq.answer: Clothes you don't mind getting dirty, closed shoes or sandals with straps, a change of clothes, a hat, sun cream and insect repellent.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated but never required. Many visitors prefer to give a donation to the sanctuary.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: All year. November to February is cool and dry; in the rainy season the valley is green and the elephants love the mud.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 72 hours before the tour, because the sanctuary fee is non-refundable after that. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
